questions.question: What is inflation?
choices: A sustained increase in the general price level
A rise in the price of only one product
A fall in every wage
A decline in total population

questions.question: What happens to a fixed amount of money's purchasing power during inflation?
choices: It generally rises
It automatically stays unchanged
It generally falls
It becomes unrelated to prices

questions.question: What is deflation?
choices: A slower rate of price increases
A sustained decrease in the general price level
A rise in all nominal wages
A decline in government borrowing only

questions.question: What is disinflation?
choices: A fall in the general price level
The elimination of all price changes
An increase in the inflation rate
A decline in the rate of inflation

questions.question: What is the Consumer Price Index designed to track?
choices: Prices paid by consumers for a representative basket
Only stock market prices
Only the value of exports
The number of unemployed workers

questions.question: What is a nominal wage?
choices: A wage adjusted for price changes
A wage paid only in goods
A wage measured in current money units
A wage guaranteed to rise with productivity

questions.question: What is a real wage?
choices: A wage before it is stated in money
A wage adjusted for purchasing power
A wage equal to total GDP
A wage earned only in manufacturing

questions.question: Why does a price rise for one product not necessarily establish general inflation?
choices: One product always represents the entire economy
Inflation is defined only by wages
Individual prices cannot change without government approval
Other prices may not be rising broadly

questions.question: How can strong demand contribute to inflation?
choices: Spending may grow faster than the economy's ability to supply output
Spending necessarily lowers every price
Demand affects only stock prices
Demand growth makes production constraints irrelevant

questions.question: How can a broad increase in energy costs contribute to inflation?
choices: Energy costs affect no other products
Higher energy costs guarantee lower transport prices
Higher costs can raise prices across many industries
Energy costs automatically increase real wages

questions.question: Why are fixed-income households vulnerable to unexpected inflation?
choices: They necessarily receive automatic price adjustments
Their income may not keep pace with rising prices
Inflation increases every household's real income
They spend no income on goods or services

questions.question: How can unexpected inflation affect a borrower with a fixed nominal debt?
choices: It automatically cancels the debt
It necessarily raises the loan's fixed interest rate
It always increases the debt's purchasing-power value
It can reduce the real burden of repayment

questions.question: Why do central banks monitor inflation expectations?
choices: Expectations can influence wage demands and price-setting
Expectations legally determine every price
Only expectations measure unemployment
Expectations replace all economic statistics

questions.question: Why can slower inflation still leave prices rising?
choices: Disinflation requires every price to fall
Inflation rates measure only production quantities
A positive inflation rate means prices continue increasing
A lower rate means all previous increases are reversed

questions.question: Why can falling prices be harmful during a severe downturn?
choices: Deflation necessarily raises every household's income
Deflation can increase real debt burdens and discourage spending
Lower prices eliminate all unemployment
Debt contracts always fall automatically with prices

questions.question: A basket costs $100 one year and $105 the next. What is its inflation rate?
A wage rises 3% while prices rise 6%. What happens approximately to purchasing power?
choices: It declines
It rises by 9%
It stays unchanged
It rises by 3%

questions.question: Inflation falls from 8% to 3% while remaining positive. Which description is correct?
choices: Deflation with prices falling
Unchanged inflation
Disinflation with prices still rising
A complete reversal of past price increases

questions.question: A loan has a 7% nominal interest rate and inflation is 4%. What is the approximate real interest rate?
Why might two households experience inflation differently?
choices: Every household buys the exact CPI basket
Only businesses face price changes
Inflation affects only imported products
They purchase different combinations of goods and services
